best_for: Composers, teachers and band arrangers who want to write and print scores without paying for Sibelius or Dorico.
description:
MuseScore Studio is a music notation app for writing sheet music, from a piano piece to a full marching band score. An open source community builds it, with more than 1,200 people translating it into 69 languages, and the website is run by MuseScore Ltd in Cyprus.

You can add lyrics, chord symbols, fingering and rehearsal marks, write for guitar, harp or percussion, and pull a separate part for each player out of the full score. Playback runs through a mixer and can use SoundFonts or VST instruments. When the score is done, you can export it as a video or publish it to MuseScore.com. The free online handbook walks you through it, from your first score to custom shortcuts and plugins.

points.title: The notation app is free
points.text: MuseScore Studio is GPL-3.0 open source and the project calls it free with no limits. Notes can be entered by mouse, keyboard or a MIDI keyboard.

points.title: Opens other people's files
points.text: MusicXML and MIDI import and export let you move scores in from and out to other notation programs and DAWs.

points.title: Better playback is a separate install
points.text: Muse Sounds, the realistic instrument library, comes through Muse Hub on Windows and Mac. On Linux it needs Muse Sounds Manager, a .deb or .rpm for x64 only, with no Arm support yet. Some extra libraries on Muse Hub are sold.

points.title: You can skip Muse Hub
points.text: The default download on Windows and Mac is the Muse Hub installer. If you only want the app, the download page also offers a plain MSI or portable build for Windows and a DMG for Mac.

points.title: Check the hardware first
points.text: The project asks for 8 GB of RAM (16 GB advised), a 4-core CPU and about 15 GB of disk if you add Muse Sounds. Windows 10 and macOS 11 are the minimums, and Muse Hub itself needs macOS 12.

points.title: Versions on each platform
points.text: Windows installs machine-wide from an MSI, and the Windows listing keeps 29 versions. Mac gets one universal DMG. The Flathub build, which Flathub does not mark as verified, is at 4.7.5 while Windows and Mac are at 4.7.7.
